issues.legal_issue: Solatium must be awarded on the full market value of compulsorily acquired land even when the landowner did not specifically claim it.
material_facts: The land was compulsorily acquired under a local improvement law that had excluded the statutory solatium available under the general land-acquisition framework.
The compensation tribunal determined the market value but did not award solatium on that amount because the landowner had not claimed it.
The appellate court awarded solatium on the additional value it assessed but not on the amount already assessed by the tribunal, also relying on the absence of a specific claim.
The exclusion of solatium under the local improvement law had been invalidated while the landowner’s appeal was pending.
issues.conclusion: Solatium had to be awarded on the entire market value, including the portion assessed by the tribunal, notwithstanding the landowner’s failure to claim it specifically.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as then in force, required the court to award solatium in every case as part of the statutory compensation for compulsory acquisition; the duty was automatic and left no discretion to deny solatium because of a procedural omission or lack of a specific claim. In Om Prakash v. State of Uttar Pradesh, [1974] 2 SCC 731, the exclusion of solatium for acquisitions under the U.P. Town Improvement Act was held discriminatory and invalid under Article 14, so compensation was to be assessed under section 23. Order 41 Rule 33 CPC also provided a means to rectify the omission in the pending appeal.

rule.if: compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appeal and applicable_scheme_requires_solatium and market_value_was_determined and solatium_was_omitted_from_part_of_market_value and claimant_did_not_specifically_claim_solatium

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appe: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for land taken compulsorily.
predicates.applicable_scheme_requires_solatium: The compensation framework applicable to the acquisition requires an additional award for the compulsory nature of the taking.
predicates.market_value_was_determined: A court or tribunal determined the market value of the acquired land.
predicates.solatium_was_omitted_from_part_of_market: The decision-maker awarded no solatium on some of the market value it determined.
predicates.claimant_did_not_specifically_claim_sola: The landowner did not specifically ask the decision-maker to award solatium.

issues.definition: When a compensation appeal concerns a compulsory acquisition for which the applicable framework requires solatium, and some determined market value was left without solatium despite no specific claim, solatium is awarded on the full market value.

issues.legal_issue: Statutory interest is payable on solatium as part of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
material_facts: The court awarded solatium on the full market value of the compulsorily acquired land.
Possession had been taken from the landowner before the solatium was paid.
The lower court had awarded interest on compensation, and the Supreme Court directed interest on the solatium from the date possession was taken until payment.
issues.conclusion: The landowner was entitled to statutory interest on the solatium from dispossession until payment.
issues.legal_principle: Solatium under section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is part of compensation, and sections 28 and 34 provide for interest on compensation. Periyar and Pareekanni Rubbers Ltd. v. State of Kerala, AIR 1990 SC 2192, recognized entitlement to interest on solatium. Although Dr. Shamlal Narula v. Commissioner of Income Tax, Punjab, [1964] 7 SCR 668, characterized statutory interest as interest for delayed payment rather than compensation for loss of possession, the Court held that solatium, being part of compensation, must bear statutory interest from dispossession until payment.

predicates.compulsory_acquisition_compensation_appe: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for land taken compulsorily.
predicates.solatium_is_awarded: The decision-maker awards an additional sum for the compulsory nature of the acquisition.
predicates.possession_was_taken_before_payment: The acquiring authority took possession of the land before paying the solatium.

issues.definition: When a compulsory-acquisition compensation appeal results in an award of solatium and possession preceded payment, statutory interest is payable on the solatium from possession until payment.
